prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary (≤500 words, policy-focused)

Economic and fiscal
- Fiscal rules: balance the current budget and have debt falling as a share of GDP by year 5; all major fiscal events scored by the OBR.
- No rises to National Insurance, basic/higher/additional Income Tax rates, or VAT. Target tax avoidance: abolish non-dom status, end IHT avoidance via offshore trusts, close carried-interest loophole, modernise and strengthen HMRC.
- Support family finances: reduce energy costs, ease food trade frictions, expand childcare access, support renters, free primary school breakfast clubs, maintain BoE 2% inflation target.

Business, industry, innovation
- Industrial Strategy with a statutory Industrial Strategy Council; sector plans (e.g., automotive, life sciences, creative, financial services).
- National Wealth Fund (£7.3bn) to crowd in private capital: ports/supply chains, gigafactories, steel, carbon capture, green hydrogen.
- Business tax stability: cap corporation tax at 25% for the parliament; retain full expensing and AIA; replace business rates in England.
- Small business: tackle late payments, reform British Business Bank, improve SME access to procurement and exports.
- Innovation: 10‑year R&D budgets for key institutions; National Data Library; Regulatory Innovation Office; binding rules for frontier AI firms; ban sexually explicit deepfakes.

Infrastructure, transport, digital
- 10‑year infrastructure strategy; National Infrastructure and Service Transformation Authority; planning reform for nationally significant projects; full gigabit and national 5G coverage by 2030.
- Roads: fix 1m extra potholes/year (A27 deferment funds); cut car insurance costs; restore 2030 ICE phase-out; accelerate EV charging; standardise used-EV battery info.
- Rail: bring passenger operations into public ownership as contracts end; GBR to integrate system; stronger freight duty and passenger watchdog.
- Buses: powers to franchise and lift municipal ownership ban; mayoral integrated transport.

Housing and planning
- 1.5m homes over the parliament; restore mandatory targets; brownfield-first with strategic “grey belt” release and “golden rules”; new towns; cross-boundary planning; more planning officers (funded via higher non‑resident SDLT surcharge).
- Boost social/affordable housing; protect new social stock; mortgage guarantee scheme; first-time buyer priority; reform compulsory purchase compensation.

Work and immigration
- New Deal for Working People: ban exploitative zero-hours contracts, end fire-and-rehire, day‑one rights to sick/parental leave and unfair dismissal protection; Single Enforcement Body; minimum wage to reflect living costs; remove age bands.
- Immigration: reduce net migration; reform points-based system; strengthen MAC; link visas to sectoral skills plans; enforce against abuse; new Border Security Command; end Rwanda scheme; clear backlog with more caseworkers; expand returns unit and EU security cooperation.

Energy, climate, environment, farming
- Clean power by 2030: double onshore wind, triple solar, quadruple offshore wind; invest in CCS, hydrogen, marine; maintain gas strategic reserve.
- Nuclear: extend existing life; deliver Hinkley and Sizewell C; support SMRs.
- North Sea: no new exploration licences; manage existing fields; ban fracking and new coal.
- Great British Energy (£8.3bn) to co‑invest in clean power; local power projects; grid upgrades; reduce standing charges.
- Warm Homes Plan: +£6.6bn to upgrade 5m homes; PRS minimum energy standards by 2030; grants/loans; no forced boiler removal.
- Carbon Border Adjustment; make UK a green finance hub with mandatory corporate transition plans.
- Nature: expand habitats, National River Walks, new National Forests; circular economy.
- Water: special measures for failing companies; stronger regulation, automatic fines, bonus blocks, independent monitoring.
- Farming: target 50% of public sector food local/certified; land-use framework; ELMs reform; TB eradication without badger cull; animal welfare bans (trail hunting, trophy imports, puppy smuggling/farming, snares).

Crime, policing, justice
- Neighbourhood Policing Guarantee: thousands of extra officers/PCSOs; national efficiency programme.
- Antisocial behaviour: Respect Orders; make offenders clean up; specific offence for assaults on shopworkers; end low‑value shoplifting “immunity”.
- Knife crime: mandatory interventions via YOTs; ban zombie/machete/ninja swords; regulate online sales; executive liability; Young Futures hubs; new offence of child criminal exploitation.
- VAWG: specialist units in every force; fast‑track rape courts; domestic abuse experts in 999; legal advocates; stronger stalking orders; spiking offence.
- Police standards: tougher HMICFRS powers; mandatory vetting/misconduct rules; strip-search safeguards; expanded fraud strategy.
- Courts/prisons: more Associate Prosecutors; victims’ protections; sentencing review; build prison places; reduce reoffending via work, housing, and joined-up probation; strategic probation review; address historical injustices (Hillsborough Law, inquiries).

Education, skills, culture, sport
- 6,500 teachers in shortage subjects; School Support Staff body; leadership programme; regional improvement teams; replace single Ofsted grade with report card; curriculum and assessment review; primary numeracy/early language focus; free primary breakfast clubs; cap uniform costs; mental health staff in every school.
- Childcare: 3,000 school‑based nurseries; parental leave review; better data-sharing; kinship/foster/adoption support.
- Post‑16: Skills England; guarantee for 18–21s (training/apprenticeship/work support); devolve adult skills; Technical Excellence Colleges; replace Apprenticeship Levy with flexible Growth & Skills Levy; stabilize HE and improve access/teaching.
- Creative industries plan; protect PE time; ticket resale protections; football regulator and fan voice.

Health and social care
- NHS: 2m extra operations/scans/appointments annually (40k/week) via overtime and independent capacity; shared waiting lists; deliver workforce plan.
- Double CT/MRI scanners; deliver New Hospitals Programme; NHS innovation/adoption strategy; enhance NHS App; maternity safety push; regulate managers; implement Cass Review recommendations.
- Primary care: more GPs; face‑to‑face on request; continuity incentives; pharmacist prescribing; broader self-referrals; pilot Neighbourhood Health Centres.
- Dentistry Rescue Plan: 700k urgent appointments; contract reform; supervised tooth‑brushing (ages 3–5).
- Social care: create a National Care Service with national standards; “home first”; NHS‑care integration for discharge; Fair Pay Agreement; guaranteed family visiting rights.
- Mental health: 8,500 extra staff; Young Futures hubs; modernise Mental Health Act; suicide prevention focus.
- Public health: generational smoking ban; restrict youth-appeal vape branding; junk-food ad ban to children; energy drink sales ban to under‑16s; strengthen online safety; gambling reforms; halve healthy life expectancy gap; new HIV action plan.

Governance, devolution, democracy
- Ethics and Integrity Commission; empower Independent Adviser; ban MPs’ paid advisory/consultancy roles; Commons Modernisation Committee.
- Lords: remove hereditary peers; retirement at 80; tighter standards/participation; consult on replacement second chamber.
- Votes at 16; improve voter registration and ID consistency; stricter donation rules.
- Reset with devolved governments; Council of the Nations and Regions; update fiscal frameworks; devolve employment support in Wales; NI: uphold Windsor Framework, repeal/replace Legacy Act.

Foreign, defence, trade
- NATO and nuclear deterrent maintained; Strategic Defence Review; path to 2.5% of GDP on defence; Armed Forces Commissioner; scrap visas for qualifying non‑UK veterans and dependants.
- Defence industrial strategy; procurement reform; support AUKUS; robust Russia stance and Ukraine support (incl. assets); balanced China approach.
- EU: stay out of single market/customs union; seek veterinary deal, MRAs, security pact; improve services mobility and touring arrangements.
- Trade: targeted FTAs and sectoral deals; WTO/CPTPP engagement; OECD global minimum tax; strategic partnership with India; Gulf and Africa strategies.
- Climate diplomacy: Clean Power Alliance; rebuild development capability; aim to restore 0.7% aid when fiscal conditions allow.
